title.zh: 卷六十三 列傳第二十三 王華 王曇首 殷景仁 沈演之
title.en: Volume 63 Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, Shen Yanzhi
title.raw: 卷六十三 列傳第二十三 王華 王曇首 殷景仁 沈演之 Volume 63 Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, Shen Yanzhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十三 王華王曇首殷景仁沈演之

translations.literal: Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, Shen Yanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 23: Wang Hua, Wang Tanshou, Yin Jingren, and Shen Yanzhi

sentences.zh: 王華，字子陵，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Hua, courtesy name Ziling, was a native of Linyi in Langya, a younger cousin of Grand Protector Hong on the paternal side.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua, whose courtesy name was Ziling, came from Linyi in Langya. He was a younger cousin of Grand Protector Wang Hong on the paternal side.

sentences.zh: 祖薈，衛將軍，會稽內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was General of the Guard and Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Hui had served as General of the Guard and Interior Minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父，廞，太子中庶子，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: His father Yin was a Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Yin had held the posts of Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 居在吳，晉隆安初，王恭起兵討王國寶，時廞丁母憂在家，恭檄令起兵，廞即聚眾應之，以女為貞烈將軍，以女人為官屬。

translations.literal: The family lived in Wu. At the beginning of the Jin Long'an era, Wang Gong raised troops to attack Wang Guobao. At that time Yin was at home observing mourning for his mother. Gong issued a summons ordering him to raise troops, and Yin immediately gathered followers to respond. He made his daughter General of Chaste Resolve and appointed women as his officials.
translations.idiomatic: The family was living in Wu when, at the start of the Jin dynasty's Long'an era, Wang Gong took up arms against Wang Guobao. Wang Yin was then at home in mourning for his mother, but when Gong's summons arrived calling on him to mobilize, he immediately gathered a force to answer it. He made his daughter General of Chaste Resolve and staffed his command with women as officials.

sentences.zh: 國寶既死，恭檄廞罷兵。

translations.literal: After Guobao was dead, Gong issued a summons ordering Yin to disband his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Guobao had been killed, Wang Gong sent a summons ordering Wang Yin to stand his troops down.

sentences.zh: 廞起兵之際，多所誅戮，至是不復得已，因舉兵以討恭為名。

translations.literal: When Yin had first raised troops he had put many people to death. By this point he could no longer stop, and so he took up arms under the pretext of attacking Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yin had first mobilized, he had executed many people. By now he could no longer simply disband, and so he raised troops again, this time under the banner of punishing Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭遣劉牢之擊廞，廞敗走，不知所在。

translations.literal: Gong sent Liu Laozhi to attack Yin. Yin was defeated and fled, and no one knew where he had gone.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong dispatched Liu Laozhi against Wang Yin. Yin was defeated and fled, and his whereabouts became unknown.

sentences.zh: 長子泰為恭所殺。

translations.literal: His eldest son Tai was killed by Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Wang Tai was killed on Wang Gong's orders.

sentences.zh: 華時年十三，在軍中，與廞相失，隨沙門釋曇永逃竄。

translations.literal: Hua was then thirteen years old and was with the army. He became separated from Yin and fled in hiding with the monk Shi Tan Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua was then only thirteen and was with the army. Separated from his father, he fled into hiding with the monk Shi Tan Yong.

sentences.zh: 時牢之搜檢覓華甚急，曇永使華提衣襆隨後，津邏咸疑焉。

translations.literal: At the time Laozhi was searching for Hua with great urgency. Tan Yong had Hua carry a bundle of clothes and follow behind him. The guards at the ferry crossings all grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi was then searching for Wang Hua with great urgency. Tan Yong had the boy carry a bundle of clothes and walk behind him, and the guards at every ferry crossing looked on with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 華行遲，永呵罵云：「奴子怠懈，行不及我！

translations.literal: Hua walked slowly. Yong shouted and cursed at him, saying, "You lazy slave boy—you cannot even keep up with me!
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hua lagged behind, Tan Yong shouted abuse at him: "You worthless, lazy wretch—you can't even keep pace with me!

sentences.zh: 」以杖捶華數十，眾乃不疑，由此得免。

translations.literal: " He beat Hua with a staff several dozen times. Only then did the crowd cease to suspect them, and in this way he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: " He then struck Wang Hua with a staff several dozen times. The onlookers no longer suspected them, and in this way the boy escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 遇赦還吳。

translations.literal: He encountered an amnesty and returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty was declared, he returned to Wu.

sentences.zh: 少有志行，以父存亡不測，布衣蔬食不交遊，如此十餘年，為時人所稱美。

translations.literal: In youth he had ambition and integrity. Because his father's fate was unknown, he wore plain clothes, ate simple food, and kept no company with others. He lived this way for more than ten years and was praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed ambition and moral resolve. With his father's fate still unknown, he dressed plainly, ate sparingly, and kept to himself for more than ten years—a conduct widely admired at the time.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲收其才用，乃發廞喪問，使華制服。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu wished to employ his talent, and so he issued notice of Yin's death and had Hua put on mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu wished to draw on his talents, and so he formally announced Wang Yin's death and had Wang Hua enter mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，高祖北伐長安，領鎮西將軍、北徐州刺史，辟華為州主簿，仍轉鎮西主簿，治中從事史，歷職著稱。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, Gaozu marched north against Chang'an and held the titles General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Northern Xuzhou. He recruited Hua as Chief Clerk of the province, then transferred him to Chief Clerk of the Guard-the-West command, and then to Registrar and Attendant Clerk. In each post he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, Emperor Gaozu marched north against Chang'an while holding the titles General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Northern Xuzhou. He recruited Wang Hua as provincial chief clerk, then transferred him to chief clerk of the Guard-the-West headquarters, and afterward to registrar and attendant clerk. In every post he distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮江陵，以為西中郎主簿，遷諮議參軍，領錄事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu was stationed at Jiangling, he appointed Hua Chief Clerk of the Western Palace Guard, then promoted him to Advisory Adjutant and put him in charge of records.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took up his post at Jiangling, he appointed Wang Hua chief clerk of the Western Palace Guard, then promoted him to advisory adjutant in charge of records.

sentences.zh: 太祖進號鎮西，復隨府轉。

translations.literal: When Taizu advanced in title to Guard-the-West, Hua again transferred with the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu was promoted to Guard-the-West, Wang Hua transferred with the headquarters once again.

sentences.zh: 太祖未親政，政事悉委司馬張邵。

translations.literal: Taizu had not yet taken personal charge of government, and all affairs were entrusted to Marshal Zhang Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu had not yet assumed personal rule, and he entrusted all government affairs to Marshal Zhang Shao.

sentences.zh: 華性尚物，不欲人在己前；

translations.literal: Hua by nature valued material display and did not wish anyone to outshine him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua was by nature fond of outward display and could not bear to let anyone outrank him in splendor.

sentences.zh: 邵性豪，每行來常引夾轂，華出入乘牽車，從者不過二三以矯之。

translations.literal: Shao was by nature extravagant. Whenever he went out he usually had paired carriages drawn up in train. Hua, entering and leaving, rode in a hand-drawn cart with no more than two or three attendants, to counter him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao was extravagant by nature and whenever he went abroad usually had paired carriages in his train. Wang Hua, by contrast, traveled in a hand-drawn cart with no more than two or three attendants—a deliberate counter to Shao's display.

sentences.zh: 嘗於城內相逢，華陽不知是邵，謂左右：「此鹵簿甚盛，必是殿下出行。

translations.literal: Once they met inside the city. Hua, in the sunlight, did not recognize that it was Shao and said to those beside him, "This guard of honor is very grand—it must be His Highness going out.
translations.idiomatic: Once, meeting inside the city, Wang Hua failed to recognize Zhang Shao in the bright light and said to his attendants, "That guard of honor is so grand—it must be His Highness going abroad.

sentences.zh: 」乃下牽車，立於道側；

translations.literal: " He then left his hand-drawn cart and stood at the side of the road.
translations.idiomatic: " He stepped down from his cart and stood aside on the road.

sentences.zh: 及邵至，乃驚。

translations.literal: When Shao arrived, he was startled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shao drew near, Wang Hua was startled to see who it was.

sentences.zh: 邵白服登城，為華所糾，坐被徵；

translations.literal: Shao went up on the city wall wearing plain white garments and was impeached by Hua. On that charge he was summoned away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shao once went up on the city wall dressed in plain white garments. Wang Hua impeached him for it, and Shao was recalled on that charge.

sentences.zh: 華代為司馬、南郡太守，行府州事。

translations.literal: Hua replaced him as Marshal and Administrator of Nan Commandery, acting in the affairs of the headquarters and the province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua replaced him as marshal and administrator of Nan Commandery, acting in the affairs of both headquarters and province.

sentences.zh: 先是，會稽孔甯子為太祖鎮西諮議參軍，以文義見賞，至是為黃門侍郎，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kong Ningzi of Kuaiji had been an Advisory Adjutant on Taizu's Guard-the-West staff and was admired for his literary learning. By this time he was a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and concurrently Colonel of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kong Ningzi of Kuaiji had served as advisory adjutant on Emperor Taizu's Guard-the-West staff and won praise for his literary learning. By this time he had become Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and concurrently Colonel of Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 甯子先為高祖太尉主簿，陳損益曰：「隆化之道，莫先於官得其才；

translations.literal: Ningzi had earlier served as Chief Clerk to Gaozu when he was Grand Commandant. He set forth proposals for improvement and loss, saying, "In the way of promoting transformation, nothing comes before putting the right talent in office.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ningzi had earlier served as chief clerk to Emperor Gaozu when he held the post of Grand Commandant. In a memorial on reforms he wrote, "In the work of elevating civilization, nothing comes before placing the right talent in office.

sentences.zh: 枚卜之方，莫若人慎其舉。

translations.literal: In the method of selection and divination, nothing is better than that men be careful in their recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: In the method of selection, nothing surpasses having men exercise care in whom they recommend.

sentences.zh: 雖復因革不同，損益有物，求賢審官，未之或改。

translations.literal: Although institutions may change with the times and gains and losses differ in substance, the pursuit of worthy men and careful appointment of officials has never been altered.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions may change with the times and reforms may differ in detail, but the pursuit of worthy men and careful appointment of officials has never changed.

sentences.zh: 師錫僉曰，煥乎欽明之誥，拔茅徵吉，著於幽《賁》之爻。

translations.literal: The Teacher's Gift and the unanimous assent shine forth in the radiant edicts of reverent brilliance; pulling up the rushes to seek the auspicious is recorded in the lines of the obscure Hexagram Adornment.
translations.idiomatic: The Teacher's Gift and unanimous assent shine forth in the radiant edicts of reverent brilliance; pulling up the rushes to seek the auspicious is recorded in the lines of the obscure Hexagram Adornment.

sentences.zh: 晉師有成，瓜衍作賞，楚乘無入，蔿賈不賀。

translations.literal: When the Jin army achieved success, rewards were granted at Guayan; when the Chu army entered without opposition, Wei Jia did not offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the army of Jin achieved victory, rewards were granted at Guayan; when the army of Chu entered without resistance, Wei Jia offered no congratulations.

sentences.zh: 今舊命惟新，幽人引領，《韶》之盡美，已備於振綱；

translations.literal: Now old appointments are made new, and reclusive men stretch their necks in expectation. The full perfection of the Sha music is already complete in the setting of the governing net.
translations.idiomatic: Now old appointments are being renewed, and reclusive men look on with eager expectation. The full perfection of the Sha music is already complete in the setting of the governing framework.

sentences.zh: 《武》之未盡，或存於理目。

translations.literal: What remains incomplete in the Wu music may still lie in the categories of principle and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: What remains incomplete in the Wu music may still lie in matters of principle and regulation.

sentences.zh: 雖九官之職，未可備舉，親民之選，尤宜在先。

translations.literal: Although the nine offices cannot all be filled at once, the selection of those who are close to the people should especially come first.
translations.idiomatic: Although not every one of the nine offices can be filled at once, the selection of officials who serve close to the people should come first.

sentences.zh: 愚欲使天朝四品官，外及守牧，各舉一人堪為二千石長吏者，以付選官，隨缺敘用，得賢受賞，失舉任罰。

translations.literal: I wish that fourth-rank officials of the court, together with prefects and governors in the provinces, each recommend one man fit to serve as a two-thousand-bushel chief administrator. These names should be sent to the selection office and used to fill vacancies as they arise. Those who gain worthy men should receive reward; those who fail in their recommendations should bear punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that every fourth-rank court official, together with every prefect and governor in the provinces, recommend one man fit to serve as a two-thousand-bushel chief administrator. The selection office should receive these names and appoint them as vacancies arise. Those who recommend worthy men should be rewarded; those who fail in their recommendations should be punished.

sentences.zh: 夫惟帝之難，豈庸識所易，然舉爾所知，非求多人，因百官之明，孰與一識之見，執咎在己，豈容徇物之私。

translations.literal: The difficulty of being the sole ruler is not something ordinary understanding can easily grasp. Yet to recommend those you know is not to seek many men. Relying on the discernment of all officials—what can compare with the insight of one who truly knows? To bear blame oneself—how could one indulge private partiality?
translations.idiomatic: The difficulty of being the sole ruler is not something ordinary understanding can easily grasp. Yet to recommend those you know is not to seek a multitude of candidates. What insight can match that of officials who truly know the men they recommend? When blame rests on oneself, how can one indulge private favoritism?

sentences.zh: 今非以選曹所銓，果於乖謬，眾職所舉，必也惟良，蓋宜使求賢辟其廣塗，考績取其少殿。

translations.literal: It is not that the Selection Bureau's assessments are bound to be wrong, nor that recommendations from all offices will necessarily be good. Rather, one should open broad paths in seeking the worthy and, in evaluating performance, take the fewest lapses as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: This is not to say that the Selection Bureau's assessments are bound to err, nor that recommendations from all offices will necessarily be good. Rather, one should open broad paths in seeking the worthy and, in evaluating performance, judge by the fewest lapses.

sentences.zh: 若才實拔群，進宜尚德，治阿之宰，不必計年，免徒之守，豈限資秩。

translations.literal: If talent and achievement stand far above the rest, promotion should honor virtue. A magistrate of Zhi'e need not be counted by years of service; a warden of Miantu should not be limited by rank and seniority.
translations.idiomatic: When talent and achievement stand far above the rest, promotion should honor virtue. A magistrate of Zhi'e need not be judged by years of service; a warden of Miantu should not be limited by rank and seniority.

sentences.zh: 自此以還，故當才均以資，資均以地。

translations.literal: From this point downward, talent and seniority should be balanced against one another, and seniority balanced against locality.
translations.idiomatic: Below that level, talent and seniority should be balanced against one another, and seniority balanced against locality.

sentences.zh: 宰蒞之官，誠曰吏職，然監觀民瘼，翼化宣風，則隱厚之求，急於刀筆，能事之功，接於德心，以此論才，行之年歲，豈惟政無秕蠹，民庇手足而已，將使公路日清，私請漸塞。

translations.literal: Magistrates who oversee districts are indeed administrative posts, yet in observing the people's afflictions and aiding transformation by spreading moral influence, the demand for hidden depth and generosity is more urgent than skill with the brush. The merit of effective service connects with the heart of virtue. To judge talent on this basis, together with years of conduct—this would not only keep government free of chaff and corruption and shelter the people like hands and feet, but would also daily clarify the public road and gradually block private requests.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who oversee districts are indeed administrative posts, yet in observing the people's afflictions and aiding moral transformation, the need for depth of character and generosity is more urgent than skill with the brush. Effective service must connect with the heart of virtue. To judge talent on this basis, together with years of conduct, would not only keep government free of corruption and shelter the people like one's own limbs, but would also daily clarify the public road and gradually choke off private solicitations.

sentences.zh: 士多心競，仁必由己，處士砥自求之節，仕子藏交馳之情。

translations.literal: When scholars compete in their hearts, benevolence must begin with oneself. Recluses will whet the integrity of self-seeking, and officeholders will hide the feelings that drive them to currying favor.
translations.idiomatic: When scholars compete in their hearts, benevolence must begin with oneself. Recluses will sharpen the integrity of self-reliance, and officeholders will conceal the eagerness that drives them to currying favor.

sentences.zh: 甯子庸微，不識治體，冒昧陳愚，退懼違謬。」

translations.literal: Ningzi is lowly and insignificant and does not understand the principles of governance. Presumptuously I state this foolish view and withdraw in fear of error."
translations.idiomatic: I, Ningzi, am lowly and insignificant and do not understand the principles of governance. Presumptuously I offer this foolish view and withdraw in fear of error."

sentences.zh: 甯子與華並有富貴之願，自羨之等秉權，日夜構之於太祖。

translations.literal: Ningzi and Hua both harbored ambitions for wealth and rank. From the time Xianzhi and the others held power, they worked day and night to undermine them before Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ningzi and Wang Hua both harbored ambitions for wealth and rank. From the time Xu Xianzhi and his faction held power, they worked day and night to undermine the two men before Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 甯子嘗東歸，至金昌亭，左右欲泊船，甯子命去之，曰：「此弑君亭，不可泊也。

translations.literal: Ningzi once returned east and came to Jinchang Pavilion. Those beside him wished to moor the boat. Ningzi ordered them away, saying, "This is the Regicide Pavilion—it cannot be moored here.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ningzi once returned east and came to Jinchang Pavilion. His attendants wished to moor the boat, but Ningzi ordered them away, saying, "This is the Regicide Pavilion—it cannot be moored here.

sentences.zh: 」華每閒居諷詠，常誦王粲《登樓賦》曰：「冀王道之一平，假高衢而騁力。

translations.literal: " Whenever Hua was at leisure at home reciting poetry, he often chanted from Wang Can's "Rhapsody on Climbing a Tower": "I hope for the royal way to be unified and level, and to borrow the high road to exert my strength.
translations.idiomatic: " In his leisure at home Wang Hua often recited Wang Can's "Rhapsody on Climbing a Tower," chanting the lines: "I hope for the royal way to be unified and level, and to borrow the high road to exert my strength.

sentences.zh: 」出入逢羨之等，每切齒憤吒，歎曰：「當見太平時不？

translations.literal: " Going out and coming in, whenever he met Xianzhi and the others he would gnash his teeth in rage and sigh, saying, "Will I ever live to see a time of peace?
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever he encountered Xu Xianzhi and his faction going out or coming in, he would gnash his teeth in rage and sigh, "Will I ever live to see a time of peace?

sentences.zh: 」元嘉二年，甯子病卒。

translations.literal: " In the second year of Yuanjia, Ningzi died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second year of Yuanjia, Kong Ningzi died of illness.

sentences.zh: 三年，誅羨之等，華遷護軍，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the third year, Xianzhi and the others were executed. Hua was transferred to General of the Guard, while remaining Gentleman Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Xu Xianzhi and his faction were executed. Wang Hua was transferred to General of the Guard while retaining his post as Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子定侯嗣，官至左衛將軍，卒。

translations.literal: His son Ding succeeded to the marquisate and rose to General of the Left Guard, then died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Ding succeeded to the marquisate, rose to the post of General of the Left Guard, and then died.

sentences.zh: 子長嗣，太宗泰始二年，坐罵母奪爵，以長弟終紹封。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded. In the second year of Taizong's Taishi era, he was stripped of his title for reviling his mother. The fief passed to Chang's younger brother Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Chang succeeded to the title. In the second year of Emperor Taizong's Taishi era, he was stripped of his rank for reviling his mother, and the fief passed to Chang's younger brother Wang Zhong.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽三年，終上表乞以封還長，許之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, Zhong submitted a memorial asking that the fief be returned to Chang. This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor, Wang Zhong submitted a memorial asking that the fief be returned to Wang Chang. The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 華從父弟鴻，五兵尚書，會稽太守。

translations.literal: Hua's younger male cousin on the paternal side, Hong, was Minister of the Five Offices of War and Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua's younger male cousin on the paternal side, Wang Hong, served as Minister of the Five Offices of War and Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 王曇首，琅邪臨沂人，太保弘少弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Tanshou was a native of Linyi in Langya and the youngest brother of Grand Protector Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanshou came from Linyi in Langya and was the youngest brother of Grand Protector Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 幼有業尚，除著作郎，不就。

translations.literal: In youth he had scholarly ambition. He was appointed Gentleman Author but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed scholarly ambition. He was appointed Gentleman Author but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 兄弟分財，曇首唯取圖書而已。

translations.literal: When the brothers divided the family property, Tanshou took only books and records.
translations.idiomatic: When the brothers divided the family property, Wang Tanshou took only books and records.

sentences.zh: 辟琅邪王大司馬屬，從府公脩復洛陽園陵。

translations.literal: He was recruited as an aide to the Grand Marshal of Langya Wang, and followed the lord of the headquarters in restoring the gardens and tombs at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as an aide to the Grand Marshal of Langya Wang and followed his lord in restoring the gardens and tombs at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 與從弟球俱詣高祖，時謝晦在坐，高祖曰：「此君並膏粱盛德，乃能屈志戎旅。

translations.literal: Together with his younger male cousin Qiu he went to see Gaozu. At the time Xie Hui was seated there. Gaozu said, "These gentlemen are both of noble lineage and lofty virtue, yet they are able to bend their wills to military service.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his younger male cousin Wang Qiu he went to see Emperor Gaozu. Xie Hui was present at the audience. Emperor Gaozu said, "These gentlemen are both of noble lineage and lofty virtue, yet they are willing to bend their wills to military service.

sentences.zh: 」曇首答曰：「既從神武之師，自使懦夫有立志。

translations.literal: " Tanshou replied, "Having followed the army of divine martial prowess, even a coward would be given firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Tanshou replied, "Having followed the army of divine martial prowess, even a coward would be given firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 」晦曰：「仁者果有勇。

translations.literal: " Hui said, "The benevolent man indeed has courage.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie Hui said, "The benevolent man indeed has courage.

sentences.zh: 」高祖悅。

translations.literal: " Gaozu was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu was pleased.

sentences.zh: 行至彭城，高祖大會戲馬台，豫坐者皆賦詩；

translations.literal: When they reached Pengcheng, Gaozu held a great gathering at the Play-Horses Terrace. All who were seated there composed poems.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Pengcheng, Emperor Gaozu held a great gathering at the Play-Horses Terrace, and all who were seated there composed poems.

sentences.zh: 曇首文先成，高祖覽讀，因問弘曰：「卿弟何如卿？

translations.literal: Tanshou's composition was finished first. Gaozu read it through and then asked Hong, "How does your younger brother compare with you?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanshou's poem was finished first. Emperor Gaozu read it through and then asked Wang Hong, "How does your younger brother compare with you?

sentences.zh: 」弘答曰：「若但如民，門戶何寄。

translations.literal: " Hong replied, "If he were merely like me, on whom would the family rely?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Hong replied, "If he were merely my equal, on whom would the family rely?

sentences.zh: 」高祖大笑。

translations.literal: " Gaozu laughed heartily.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu laughed heartily.

sentences.zh: 曇首有識局智度，喜慍不見於色，閨門之內，雍雍如也。

translations.literal: Tanshou had discernment, breadth of vision, and wisdom. Joy and anger did not show on his face. Within the inner quarters of his household, all was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanshou possessed discernment, breadth of vision, and wisdom. Joy and anger never showed on his face, and within his household all was harmonious.

sentences.zh: 手不執金玉，婦女不得為飾玩，自非祿賜所及，一毫不受於人。

translations.literal: His hand did not hold gold or jade. The women of the household were not allowed ornamental trinkets. Apart from salary and gifts from the throne, he did not accept the slightest thing from others.
translations.idiomatic: He would not handle gold or jade, and the women of his household were forbidden ornamental trinkets. Apart from salary and gifts from the throne, he would not accept the slightest thing from anyone.

sentences.zh: 太祖為冠軍、徐州刺史，留鎮彭城，以曇首為府功曹。

translations.literal: When Taizu was Champion General and Inspector of Xuzhou, he remained stationed at Pengcheng and appointed Tanshou Chief Clerk of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu was Champion General and Inspector of Xuzhou, he remained stationed at Pengcheng and appointed Wang Tanshou chief clerk of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮江陵，自功曹為長史，隨府轉鎮西長史。

translations.literal: When Taizu was stationed at Jiangling, Tanshou rose from Chief Clerk to Chief Administrator, and then transferred with the headquarters to become Chief Administrator of Guard-the-West.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took up his post at Jiangling, Wang Tanshou rose from chief clerk to chief administrator, then transferred with the headquarters to become chief administrator of Guard-the-West.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚知之，謂太祖曰：「王曇首，沈毅有器度，宰相才也。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew him very well and said to Taizu, "Wang Tanshou is steady, resolute, and possessed of breadth of character. He has the talent of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu knew him well and said to Emperor Taizu, "Wang Tanshou is steady, resolute, and possessed of breadth of character. He has the talent of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 汝每事咨之。

translations.literal: In every matter you should consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Consult him in every matter.

sentences.zh: 」景平中，有龍見西方，半天騰上，廕五彩雲，京都遠近聚觀，太史奏曰：「西方有天子氣。

translations.literal: " In the Jingping era a dragon appeared in the west, soaring halfway up the sky and shaded by five-colored clouds. People near and far in the capital gathered to watch. The Grand Astrologer memorialized, saying, "In the west there is the aura of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Jingping era a dragon appeared in the west, soaring halfway up the sky beneath five-colored clouds. People throughout the capital gathered to watch. The Grand Astrologer memorialized, "In the west there is the aura of the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」太祖入奉大統，上及議者皆疑不敢下，曇首與到彥之、從兄華固勸，上猶未許。

translations.literal: " Taizu entered the capital to receive the great succession. The emperor and those who deliberated with him all hesitated and dared not descend. Tanshou, together with Dao Yanzhi and his older male cousin Hua, firmly urged him on, but the emperor still did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Taizu entered the capital to receive the great succession. The emperor and his advisers all hesitated and dared not proceed. Wang Tanshou, together with Dao Yanzhi and his older male cousin Wang Hua, firmly urged him on, but the emperor still would not consent.

sentences.zh: 曇首又固陳，並言天人符應，上乃下。

translations.literal: Tanshou again pressed his case firmly, also speaking of the correspondence between Heaven and man. Only then did the emperor descend.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanshou pressed his case again, citing the correspondence between Heaven and man, and only then did the emperor proceed.

sentences.zh: 率府州文武嚴兵自衛，臺所遣百官眾力，不得近部伍，中兵參軍朱容子抱刀在平乘戶外，不解帶者數旬。

translations.literal: He led the civil and military officials of the headquarters and province in strict self-defense with armed troops. The officials and forces sent from the capital were not allowed near his ranks. The Middle Army Adjutant Zhu Rongzi, holding a sword, stood outside the Pingcheng gate and did not ungird his blade for several tens of days.
translations.idiomatic: He led the civil and military officials of headquarters and province in strict self-defense with armed troops. The officials and forces sent from the capital were not allowed near his ranks. The middle army adjutant Zhu Rongzi stood outside the Pingcheng gate with sword in hand and did not ungird his blade for several tens of days.

sentences.zh: 既下在道，有黃龍出負上所乘舟，左右皆失色，上謂曇首曰：「此乃夏禹所以受天命，我何堪之。

translations.literal: After he had descended and was on the road, a yellow dragon appeared and bore up the boat on which the emperor was riding. Those beside him all changed color in alarm. The emperor said to Tanshou, "This is how Yu of Xia received the Mandate of Heaven—how could I be worthy of it?
translations.idiomatic: After he had set out on the road, a yellow dragon appeared and bore up the boat on which the emperor was riding. His attendants all paled in alarm. The emperor said to Wang Tanshou, "This is how Yu of Xia received the Mandate of Heaven—how could I be worthy of it?

sentences.zh: 」及即位，又謂曇首曰：「非宋昌獨見，無以致此。

translations.literal: " When he took the throne, he again said to Tanshou, "Had it not been for Song Chang's lone insight, this could not have been achieved.
translations.idiomatic: " When he took the throne, he again said to Wang Tanshou, "Had it not been for Song Chang's lone insight, this could not have been achieved.

sentences.zh: 」以曇首為侍中，尋領右衛將軍，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: " He appointed Tanshou Gentleman Attendant, and soon afterward made him concurrently General of the Right Guard and General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " He appointed Wang Tanshou Gentleman Attendant, and soon afterward made him concurrently General of the Right Guard and General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以朱容子為右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He appointed Zhu Rongzi General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhu Rongzi General of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 誅徐羨之等，平謝晦，曇首及華之力也。

translations.literal: The execution of Xu Xianzhi and the others and the pacification of Xie Hui were due to the efforts of Tanshou and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The execution of Xu Xianzhi and his faction and the pacification of Xie Hui were due to the efforts of Wang Tanshou and Wang Hua.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年，車駕出北堂，嘗使三更竟開廣莫門，南臺云：「應須白虎幡，銀字棨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia the imperial carriage went out through the North Hall. An order was once sent at the end of the third watch to open the Broad Mo Gate. The Southern Office said, "The white tiger banner and the silver-character signal staff are required.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia the imperial carriage went out through the North Hall. An order was once sent at the end of the third watch to open the Broad Mo Gate. The Southern Office replied, "The white tiger banner and the silver-character signal staff are required.

sentences.zh: 」不肯開門。

translations.literal: " They refused to open the gate.
translations.idiomatic: " They refused to open the gate.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞羊玄保奏免御史中丞傅隆以下，曇首繼啟曰：「既無墨敕，又闕幡棨，雖稱上旨，不異單刺。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Yang Xuanbao memorialized to dismiss the Censor-in-Chief Fu Long and those below him. Tanshou followed with a memorial, saying, "Since there was neither an ink edict nor the banner and staff, although it was said to carry the emperor's intent, it was no different from a private note.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat Yang Xuanbao memorialized to dismiss Censor-in-Chief Fu Long and those below him. Wang Tanshou followed with a memorial saying, "Since there was neither an ink edict nor the banner and staff, although the order claimed to carry the emperor's intent, it was no different from a private note.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年、二年，雖有再開門例，此乃前事之違。

translations.literal: In the first and second years of Yuanjia there were precedents for opening the gate a second time, but those were violations of earlier practice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first and second years of Yuanjia there were precedents for opening the gate a second time, but those were departures from proper practice.

sentences.zh: 今之守舊，未為非禮。

translations.literal: The present adherence to old rules is not contrary to propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The present adherence to established rules is not contrary to propriety.

sentences.zh: 但既據舊史，應有疑卻本末，曾無此狀，猶宜反咎其不請白虎幡、銀字棨，致門不時開，由尚書相承之失，亦合糾正。

translations.literal: Yet since they relied on old records, there should have been a full account of the grounds for hesitation and refusal. Since there was no such record, they should instead be blamed for not requesting the white tiger banner and silver-character staff, which caused the gate not to open in time. This was a failure handed down through the Secretariat and should also be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since they relied on established records, there should have been a full account of the grounds for hesitation and refusal. Since there was no such record, blame should instead fall on them for failing to request the white tiger banner and silver-character staff, which caused the gate not to open in time. This was a failure handed down through the Secretariat and should also be corrected.

sentences.zh: 」上特無所問，更立科條。

translations.literal: " The emperor specially made no inquiries and instead established new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor made no further inquiries and instead established new regulations.

sentences.zh: 遷太子詹事，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince while remaining Gentleman Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince while retaining his post as Gentleman Attendant.

sentences.zh: 晦平後，上欲封曇首等，會宴集，舉酒勸之，因拊御床曰：「此坐非卿兄弟，無復今日。

translations.literal: After Hui was pacified, the emperor wished to ennoble Tanshou and the others. At a banquet gathering he raised his cup to urge them on and, patting the imperial couch, said, "Had it not been for you brothers in this seat, there would be no today.
translations.idiomatic: After Xie Hui was pacified, the emperor wished to ennoble Wang Tanshou and the others. At a banquet he raised his cup to urge them on and, patting the imperial couch, said, "Had it not been for you brothers in this seat, there would be no today.

sentences.zh: 」時封詔已成，出以示曇首，曇首曰：「近日之事，釁難將成，賴陛下英明速斷，故罪人斯戮。

translations.literal: " At the time the enfeoffment edict had already been completed. The emperor produced it and showed it to Tanshou. Tanshou said, "In recent affairs disaster was about to take shape. It was thanks to Your Majesty's brilliant and swift decision that the guilty were thus punished.
translations.idiomatic: " The enfeoffment edict had already been completed. The emperor produced it and showed it to Wang Tanshou. Tanshou said, "In recent affairs disaster was about to take shape. It was thanks to Your Majesty's brilliant and swift decision that the guilty were punished.

sentences.zh: 臣等雖得仰憑天光，效其毫露，豈可因國之災，以為身幸。

translations.literal: Although we your ministers were able to rely on Heaven's radiance and offer our tiny contribution, how could we turn the state's disaster into personal good fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Although we your ministers were able to rely on Heaven's radiance and offer our tiny contribution, how could we turn the state's disaster into personal good fortune?

sentences.zh: 陛下雖欲私臣，當如直史何？

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty wished to favor us ministers, what of the upright historiographers?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty wished to favor us ministers, what of the upright historiographers?

sentences.zh: 」上不能奪，故封事遂寢。

translations.literal: " The emperor could not override him, and so the matter of enfeoffment was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor could not override him, and so the matter of enfeoffment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時兄弘錄尚書事，又為揚州刺史，曇首為上所親委，任兼兩宮。

translations.literal: At the time his older brother Hong recorded the affairs of the Masters of Writing and also served as Inspector of Yangzhou. Tanshou was personally entrusted by the emperor and held responsibilities spanning both palaces.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his older brother Wang Hong recorded the affairs of the Masters of Writing and also served as Inspector of Yangzhou. Wang Tanshou was personally entrusted by the emperor and held responsibilities spanning both palaces.

sentences.zh: 彭城王義康與弘並錄，意常怏怏，又欲得揚州，形於辭旨。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Yikang recorded affairs together with Hong and was often discontented in mind. He also wished to obtain Yangzhou, and this showed in his words.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Liu Yikang recorded affairs together with Wang Hong and was often discontented. He also wished to obtain Yangzhou, and this showed plainly in his words.

sentences.zh: 以曇首居中，分其權任，愈不悅。

translations.literal: Because Tanshou stood at the center and divided his power and responsibilities, he became all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wang Tanshou stood at the center and divided his power and responsibilities, Yikang became all the more displeased.

sentences.zh: 曇首固乞吳郡，太祖曰：「豈有欲建大廈而遺其棟樑者哉？

translations.literal: Tanshou firmly begged to be sent to Wu Commandery. Taizu said, "How could one wish to build a great hall yet leave aside its pillars and beams?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanshou firmly begged to be sent to Wu Commandery. Emperor Taizu said, "How could one wish to build a great hall yet leave aside its pillars and beams?

sentences.zh: 賢兄比屢稱疾，固辭州任，將來若相申許者，此處非卿而誰？

translations.literal: Your worthy older brother has repeatedly claimed illness and firmly declined the provincial post. If in the future he should be granted his request, who but you should hold this place?
translations.idiomatic: Your worthy older brother has repeatedly claimed illness and firmly declined the provincial post. If in the future he should be granted his request, who but you should hold this place?

sentences.zh: 亦何吳郡之有。

translations.literal: What need is there for Wu Commandery?
translations.idiomatic: What need is there for Wu Commandery?

sentences.zh: 」時弘久疾，屢遜位，不許。

translations.literal: " At the time Hong had long been ill and repeatedly yielded his post, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Wang Hong had long been ill and repeatedly asked to resign, but each request was refused.

sentences.zh: 義康謂賓客曰：「王公久疾不起，神州詎合臥治。

translations.literal: Yikang said to his guests, "Lord Wang has long been ill and cannot rise. How can the heartland be governed from one's bed?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikang said to his guests, "Lord Wang has long been ill and cannot rise. How can the heartland be governed from one's sickbed?

sentences.zh: 」曇首勸弘減府兵力之半以配義康，義康乃悅。

translations.literal: " Tanshou urged Hong to reduce the headquarters' military strength by half and assign it to Yikang. Only then was Yikang pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Tanshou urged Wang Hong to cut the headquarters' military strength in half and assign it to Liu Yikang. Only then was Yikang pleased.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 太祖為之慟，中書舍人周赳侍側，曰：「王家欲衰，賢者先殞。

translations.literal: Taizu grieved deeply for him. Palace Secretary Attendant Zhou Jiu, attending at his side, said, "The Wang house is about to decline—the worthy die first.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu grieved deeply for him. Palace Secretary Attendant Zhou Jiu, attending at his side, said, "The Wang house is about to decline—the worthy die first.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「直是我家衰耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "It is simply that my own house is declining.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "It is simply that my own house is declining.

sentences.zh: 」追贈左光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，詹事如故。

translations.literal: " Posthumously he was granted Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and additionally made Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, while retaining his post as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: " Posthumously he was granted Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and additionally made Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, while retaining his post as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 九年，以預誅羨之等謀，追封豫寧縣侯，邑千戶，諡曰文侯。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, because he had taken part in the plot to execute Xianzhi and the others, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Yunin with a fief of one thousand households. His posthumous title was Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, because he had taken part in the plot to execute Xu Xianzhi and his faction, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Yunin with a fief of one thousand households. His posthumous title was Marquis Wen.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，配饗太祖廟庭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, Tanshou was given a place in the sacrifices at Taizu's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, Wang Tanshou was given a place in the sacrifices at Emperor Taizu's temple hall.

sentences.zh: 子僧綽嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Sengchuo succeeded. He has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Sengchuo succeeded to the title. He has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 少子僧虔，昇明末，為尚書令。

translations.literal: His youngest son Sengqian, at the end of the Shengming era, became Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Wang Sengqian, at the end of the Shengming era, became Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 殷景仁，陳郡長平人也。

translations.literal: Yin Jingren was a native of Changping in Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jingren came from Changping in Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖融，晉太常。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rong was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yin Rong had served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness under the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 祖茂，散騎常侍、特進、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao was Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, Special Advance, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yin Mao had held the posts of Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry, Special Advance, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 父道裕，蚤亡。

translations.literal: His father Daoyu died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin Daoyu died young.

sentences.zh: 景仁少有大成之量，司徒王謐見而以女妻之。

translations.literal: Jingren in youth had the capacity for great achievement. Minister of Education Wang Mi saw this and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yin Jingren showed the capacity for great achievement. Minister of Education Wang Mi recognized it and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 初為劉毅後軍參軍，高祖太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: At first he served as Rear Army Adjutant under Liu Yi and as Acting Adjutant to Gaozu when he was Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as rear army adjutant under Liu Yi and as acting adjutant to Emperor Gaozu when he held the post of Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 建議宜令百官舉才，以所薦能否為黜陟。

translations.literal: He proposed that all officials should be ordered to recommend talent, and that promotion and demotion should be based on whether those recommended proved able or not.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that all officials be required to recommend talent, with promotion and demotion determined by whether those recommended proved able or not.

sentences.zh: 遷宋臺秘書郎，世子中軍參軍，轉主簿，又為驃騎將軍道憐主簿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat on the Song Terrace, Middle Army Adjutant to the Heir Apparent, then Chief Clerk, and then Chief Clerk to Swift Cavalry General Daolian.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat on the Song Terrace, middle army adjutant to the Heir Apparent, then chief clerk, and afterward chief clerk to Swift Cavalry General Daolian.

sentences.zh: 出補衡陽太守，入為宋世子洗馬，仍轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He went out to fill the post of Administrator of Hengyang, then entered court as Groom of the Heir Apparent of Song, and was then transferred to Gentleman Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as Administrator of Hengyang, then entered court as groom of the Heir Apparent of Song, and was afterward transferred to Gentleman Attendant of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 景仁學不為文，敏有思致，口不談義，深達理體；

translations.literal: Jingren did not pursue learning for the sake of literary composition. He was quick and possessed thoughtful insight. He did not speak of abstruse doctrine, yet he deeply understood fundamental principles.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jingren did not pursue learning for the sake of literary composition. He was quick-witted and possessed thoughtful insight. He did not discourse on abstruse doctrine, yet he deeply understood fundamental principles.

sentences.zh: 至於國典朝儀，舊章記注，莫不撰錄，識者知其有當世之志也。

translations.literal: As for state codes, court ritual, old regulations, and recorded annotations, there was none he did not compile and record. Those who understood him knew that he harbored ambitions for the age.
translations.idiomatic: As for state codes, court ritual, old regulations, and recorded annotations, there was none he did not compile and record. Those who understood him knew that he harbored ambitions to serve the age.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚知之，遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew him very well and transferred him to Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu knew him well and transferred him to Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 太祖所生章太后早亡，上奉太后所生蘇氏甚謹。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhang, who had borne Taizu, died early. The emperor served Lady Su, who had borne the empress dowager, with great reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhang, who had borne Emperor Taizu, died early. The emperor served Lady Su, who had borne the empress dowager, with great reverence.

sentences.zh: 六年，蘇氏卒，車駕親往臨哭，下詔曰：「朕夙罹偏罰，情事兼常，每思有以光隆懿戚，少申罔極之懷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Lady Su died. The imperial carriage went in person to mourn at her deathbed. An edict was issued, saying, "From early on I have suffered partial loss, and my feelings are doubly ordinary. I have always thought to glorify my honored kin and give some expression to boundless grief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Lady Su died. The emperor went in person to mourn at her deathbed. An edict was issued, saying, "From early on I have suffered partial loss, and my feelings are doubly ordinary. I have always wished to glorify my honored kin and give some expression to boundless grief.

sentences.zh: 而禮文遺逸，取正無所，監之前代，用否又殊，故惟疑累年，在心未遂。

translations.literal: Yet the ritual texts have been lost and scattered, and there is nowhere to seek proper standards. Looking to earlier ages, what was adopted or rejected differs again. Therefore I have hesitated for years, and what is in my heart remains unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ritual texts have been lost and scattered, and there is nowhere to seek proper standards. Looking to earlier ages, what was adopted or rejected differs again. Therefore I have hesitated for years, and what is in my heart remains unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 蘇夫人奄至傾殂，情禮莫寄，追思遠恨，與事而深，日月有期，將卜窀穸，便欲粗依《春秋》以貴之義，式遵二漢推恩之典。

translations.literal: Lady Su has suddenly fallen and died. Feeling and ritual have nowhere to lodge. Recalling distant regrets, my sorrow grows with the event. The days and months have their term, and burial is soon to be divined. I wish roughly to follow the Spring and Autumn Annals in the principle of honoring by rank, and to model myself on the Han dynasties' precedent of extending grace.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Su has suddenly fallen and died. Feeling and ritual have nowhere to lodge. Recalling distant regrets, my sorrow grows with the event. The days and months have their term, and burial is soon to be divined. I wish roughly to follow the Spring and Autumn Annals in the principle of honoring by rank, and to model myself on the Han dynasties' precedent of extending grace.

sentences.zh: 但動藉史筆，傳之後昆，稱心而行，或容未允。

translations.literal: Yet every action rests on the historiographer's brush and is transmitted to later generations. To act as the heart desires may perhaps not be fully acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every action rests on the historiographer's brush and is transmitted to later generations. To act as the heart desires may perhaps not be fully acceptable.

sentences.zh: 可時共詳論，以求其中。

translations.literal: You may now discuss this together in detail to seek the proper middle course.
translations.idiomatic: Discuss this together in detail now to seek the proper middle course.

sentences.zh: 執筆永懷，益增感塞。

translations.literal: Holding the brush, I cherish this memory forever, and my feeling of being moved and blocked only increases.
translations.idiomatic: Holding the brush, I cherish this memory forever, and my feeling of being moved and overwhelmed only increases.

sentences.zh: 」景仁議曰：「至德之感，靈啟厥祥，文母俔天，實熙皇祚。

translations.literal: " Jingren submitted his opinion, saying, "The response of supreme virtue moves the spirits and opens auspicious signs. The civil mother matches Heaven and truly glorifies the imperial fortune.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin Jingren submitted his opinion, saying, "The response of supreme virtue moves the spirits and opens auspicious signs. The civil mother matches Heaven and truly glorifies the imperial fortune.

sentences.zh: 主上聿遵先典，號極徽崇，以貴之義，禮盡於此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty reverently follows the former canon, and in title reaches the utmost honor and elevation. In the principle of honoring by rank, ritual is complete in this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reverently follows the former canon, and in title reaches the utmost honor and elevation. In the principle of honoring by rank, ritual is complete in this.

sentences.zh: 蘇夫人階緣戚屬，情以事深，寒泉之思，實感聖懷，明詔爰發，詢求厥中。

translations.literal: Lady Su, by the steps of kinship, is related as a kinswoman. Feeling runs deep because of the matter. The thought of the cold spring truly moves the sacred heart. A bright edict has been issued seeking the proper middle course.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Su stands in the steps of kinship as a kinswoman. Feeling runs deep because of the matter. The thought of the cold spring truly moves the sacred heart. A bright edict has been issued seeking the proper middle course.

sentences.zh: 謹尋漢氏推恩加爵，於時承秦之弊，儒術蔑如，自君作故，罔或前典，懼非盛明所宜軌蹈。

translations.literal: Carefully examining the Han practice of extending grace and adding noble rank: at that time they inherited the defects of Qin, and Confucian learning was scorned. The ruler made new precedents, with no former canon to follow. I fear this is not a path our flourishing clarity should tread.
translations.idiomatic: Carefully examining the Han practice of extending grace and adding noble rank: at that time they inherited the defects of Qin, and Confucian learning was scorned. The ruler made new precedents with no former canon to follow. I fear this is not a path our flourishing clarity should tread.

sentences.zh: 晉監二代，朝政之所因，君舉必書，哲王之所慎。

translations.literal: Jin observed the two earlier dynasties and took its court governance from them. Every action of the ruler must be recorded—this is what the wise kings were careful about.
translations.idiomatic: Jin observed the two earlier dynasties and took its court governance from them. Every action of the ruler must be recorded—this is what the wise kings were careful about.

sentences.zh: 體至公者，懸爵賞於無私；

translations.literal: Embodying utmost fairness means suspending rank and reward upon impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: Embodying utmost fairness means suspending rank and reward upon impartiality.

sentences.zh: 奉天統者，每屈情以申制。

translations.literal: Upholding the mandate of Heaven means often bending personal feeling to assert regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Upholding the mandate of Heaven means often bending personal feeling to assert regulation.

sentences.zh: 所以作孚萬國，貽則後昆。

translations.literal: In this way one inspires trust throughout the myriad states and leaves a model for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: In this way one inspires trust throughout the myriad states and leaves a model for later generations.

sentences.zh: 臣豫蒙博逮，謹露庸短。

translations.literal: Your minister has undeservedly received broad instruction and humbly offers this mediocre view.
translations.idiomatic: Your minister has undeservedly received broad instruction and humbly offers this mediocre view.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，葬竟，起為領軍將軍，固辭。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his mother and after the burial, he was recalled to serve as General of the Guard. He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Upon completing mourning for his mother and after the burial, he was recalled to serve as General of the Guard. He firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 上使綱紀代拜，遣中書舍人周赳輿載還府。

translations.literal: The emperor had the household steward perform the bow in his place and sent Palace Secretary Attendant Zhou Jiu in a carriage to bring him back to his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the household steward perform the bow in his place and sent Palace Secretary Attendant Zhou Jiu in a carriage to bring him back to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 九年，服闋，遷尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when his mourning ended, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when his mourning ended, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事劉湛代為領軍，與景仁素善，皆被遇於高祖，俱以宰相許之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince Liu Zhan replaced him as General of the Guard. Zhan and Jingren had long been on good terms. Both had been favored by Gaozu, and both were regarded as future chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince Liu Zhan replaced him as General of the Guard. Zhan and Yin Jingren had long been on good terms. Both had been favored by Emperor Gaozu, and both were regarded as future chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 湛尚居外任，會王弘、華、曇首相係亡，景仁引湛還朝，共參政事。

translations.literal: Zhan was still serving in an outside post. When Wang Hong, Hua, and Tanshou died one after another, Jingren brought Zhan back to court to participate jointly in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan was still serving in an outside post. When Wang Hong, Wang Hua, and Wang Tanshou died one after another, Yin Jingren brought Zhan back to court to participate jointly in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 湛既入，以景仁位遇本不逾己，而一旦居前，意甚憤憤。

translations.literal: Once Zhan had entered court, he felt that Jingren's rank and treatment had originally not exceeded his own, yet Jingren had suddenly moved ahead of him. He was deeply resentful in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Zhan had entered court, he felt that Yin Jingren's rank and treatment had originally not exceeded his own, yet Jingren had suddenly moved ahead of him. He was deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 知太祖信仗景仁，不可移奪，乃深結司徒彭城王義康，欲倚宰相之重以傾之。

translations.literal: Knowing that Taizu trusted and relied on Jingren and that this could not be shifted or taken away, he formed a deep alliance with Minister of Education Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, wishing to lean on the weight of a chief minister to bring Jingren down.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Emperor Taizu trusted and relied on Yin Jingren and that this could not be shifted, he formed a deep alliance with Minister of Education Prince of Pengcheng Liu Yikang, wishing to lean on the weight of a chief minister to bring Jingren down.

sentences.zh: 十二年，景仁復遷中書令，護軍、僕射如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Jingren was again transferred to Director of the Central Secretariat, while retaining his posts as Protector of the Army and Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Yin Jingren was again transferred to Director of the Central Secretariat, while retaining his posts as Protector of the Army and Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 尋復以僕射領吏部，護軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again served as Vice Director while heading the Ministry of Personnel, and remained Protector of the Army as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he again served as Vice Director while heading the Ministry of Personnel, and remained Protector of the Army as before.

sentences.zh: 湛愈忿怒。

translations.literal: Zhan grew all the more angry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan grew all the more angry.

sentences.zh: 義康納湛言，毀景仁於太祖；

translations.literal: Yikang accepted Zhan's words and slandered Jingren before Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yikang accepted Liu Zhan's words and slandered Yin Jingren before Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖遇之益隆。

translations.literal: Taizu treated Jingren with ever greater favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu treated Yin Jingren with ever greater favor.

sentences.zh: 景仁對親舊歎曰：「引之令入，入便噬人。

translations.literal: Jingren said to relatives and old friends with a sigh, "I brought him in, and once inside he bites people.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jingren said to relatives and old friends with a sigh, "I brought him in, and once inside he bites people.

sentences.zh: 」乃稱疾解職，表疏累上，不見許，使停家養病。

translations.literal: " He then claimed illness and resigned his post. Memorial after memorial was submitted, but none was granted. He was ordered to remain at home and convalesce.
translations.idiomatic: " He then claimed illness and resigned his post. Memorial after memorial was submitted, but none was granted. He was ordered to remain at home and convalesce.

sentences.zh: 發詔遣黃門侍郎省疾。

translations.literal: An edict was issued sending a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate to inquire after his illness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued sending a Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate to inquire after his illness.

sentences.zh: 湛議遣人若劫盜者於外殺之，以為太祖雖知，當有以，終不能傷至親之愛。

translations.literal: Zhan proposed sending men disguised as robbers to kill him outside, reasoning that even if Taizu knew, he would have his reasons and in the end could not wound the love between the closest of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan proposed sending men disguised as robbers to kill him outside, reasoning that even if Emperor Taizu knew, he would have his reasons and in the end could not wound the love between the closest of kin.

sentences.zh: 上微聞之，遷景仁於西掖門外晉鄱陽主第，以為護軍府，密邇宮禁，故其計不行。

translations.literal: The emperor faintly heard of this and transferred Jingren to the residence of the Jin Princess of Poyang outside the Western Side Gate, making it his Protector-of-the-Army headquarters. It was close to the palace precincts, and so their plan could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor faintly heard of this and transferred Yin Jingren to the residence of the Jin Princess of Poyang outside the Western Side Gate, making it his Protector-of-the-Army headquarters. It was close to the palace precincts, and so their plan could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 景仁臥疾者五年，雖不見上，而密表去來，日中以十數；

translations.literal: Jingren lay ill for five years. Although he did not see the emperor, secret memorials went back and forth, numbering in the tens each day at midday.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Jingren lay ill for five years. Although he did not see the emperor, secret memorials went back and forth, numbering in the tens each day at midday.

sentences.zh: 朝政大小，必以問焉，影跡周密，莫有窺其際者。

translations.literal: Great and small matters of court governance were invariably referred to him. The traces were closely guarded, and no one could peer into their inner workings.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small matters of court governance were invariably referred to him. The traces were closely guarded, and no one could peer into their inner workings.

sentences.zh: 收湛之日，景仁使拂拭衣冠，寢疾既久，左右皆不曉其意。

translations.literal: On the day Zhan was arrested, Jingren had his robes and cap brushed clean. He had long been bedridden with illness, and those beside him did not understand his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Liu Zhan was arrested, Yin Jingren had his robes and cap brushed clean. He had long been bedridden with illness, and those beside him did not understand his meaning.

sentences.zh: 其夜，上出華林園延賢堂召景仁，猶稱腳疾，小床輿以就坐，誅討處分，一皆委之。

translations.literal: That night the emperor went out to the Hall for Extending Worthies in the Hualin Garden and summoned Jingren. Jingren still claimed illness in his feet and was brought in a small bed-cart to take his seat. All decisions on punishment and disposition were entirely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor went out to the Hall for Extending Worthies in the Hualin Garden and summoned Yin Jingren. Jingren still claimed illness in his feet and was brought in a small bed-cart to take his seat. All decisions on punishment and disposition were entirely entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 代義康為揚州刺史，僕射領吏部如故。

translations.literal: He replaced Yikang as Inspector of Yangzhou, while remaining Vice Director and head of the Ministry of Personnel as before.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Liu Yikang as Inspector of Yangzhou, while remaining Vice Director and head of the Ministry of Personnel as before.

sentences.zh: 遣使者授印綬，主簿代拜，拜畢，便覺其情理乖錯。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to confer the seal and cord. The chief clerk performed the bow in his place. When the bow was finished, he immediately felt that his mind and feelings had gone awry.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was sent to confer the seal and cord. The chief clerk performed the bow in his place. When the bow was finished, he immediately felt that his mind and feelings had gone awry.

sentences.zh: 性本寬厚，而忽更苛暴，問左右曰：「今年男婚多？

translations.literal: By nature he had been generous and mild, but he suddenly became harsh and violent. He asked those beside him, "This year are there more male marriages?
translations.idiomatic: By nature he had been generous and mild, but he suddenly became harsh and violent. He asked those beside him, "This year are there more male marriages?

sentences.zh: 女嫁多？

translations.literal: Or more female marriages?
translations.idiomatic: Or more female marriages?

sentences.zh: 」是冬大雪，景仁乘輿出聽事觀望，忽驚曰：「當閣何得有大樹？

translations.literal: " That winter there was heavy snow. Jingren rode in his carriage out to the office hall to look around and suddenly cried out in alarm, "How can there be a great tree blocking the gate?
translations.idiomatic: " That winter there was heavy snow. Yin Jingren rode in his carriage out to the office hall to look around and suddenly cried out in alarm, "How can there be a great tree blocking the gate?

sentences.zh: 」既而曰：「我誤邪？

translations.literal: " Then he said, "Was I mistaken?
translations.idiomatic: " Then he said, "Was I mistaken?

sentences.zh: 」疾轉篤。

translations.literal: " His illness grew critically severe.
translations.idiomatic: " His illness grew critically severe.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂不利在州司，使還住僕射下省，為州凡月餘卒。

translations.literal: Taizu said that holding the provincial post was unfavorable and had him return to lodge at the Vice Director's lower office. He had held the province for little more than a month in all before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu said that holding the provincial post was unfavorable and had him return to lodge at the Vice Director's lower office. He had held the province for little more than a month in all before he died.

sentences.zh: 或云見劉湛為祟。

translations.literal: Some said he had seen Liu Zhan haunting him.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he had seen Liu Zhan haunting him.

sentences.zh: 時年五十一，追贈侍中、司空，本官如故。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-one years old. Posthumously he was granted Gentleman Attendant and Minister of Works, while his original posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then fifty-one years old. Posthumously he was granted Gentleman Attendant and Minister of Works, while his original posts remained as before.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文成公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Wen of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Duke Wen of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 上與荊州刺史衡陽王義季書曰：「殷僕射疾患少日，奄忽不救。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote to Prince of Hengyang Yiji, Inspector of Jingzhou, saying, "Vice Director Yin was ill for only a few days and then suddenly could not be saved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote to Prince of Hengyang Liu Yiji, Inspector of Jingzhou, saying, "Vice Director Yin was ill for only a few days and then suddenly could not be saved.

sentences.zh: 其識具經遠，奉國竭誠，周遊繾綣，情兼常痛。

translations.literal: His knowledge was comprehensive, his vision far-reaching, and his service to the state utterly sincere. Our long intimacy fills me with ordinary grief redoubled.
translations.idiomatic: His knowledge was comprehensive, his vision far-reaching, and his service to the state utterly sincere. Our long intimacy fills me with grief redoubled.

sentences.zh: 民望國器，遇之為難，惋歎之深，不能已已。

translations.literal: He was the people's hope and the state's vessel. To encounter such a man is rare. My regret and sighing run so deep they cannot cease.
translations.idiomatic: He was the people's hope and the state's pillar. To encounter such a man is rare. My regret and sighing run so deep they cannot cease.

sentences.zh: 汝亦同不？

translations.literal: Do you feel the same?
translations.idiomatic: Do you feel the same?

sentences.zh: 往矣如何！

translations.literal: He is gone—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: He is gone—what can be done!

sentences.zh: 」世祖大明五年，行幸經景仁墓，詔曰：「司空文成公景仁德量淹正，風識明允，徽績忠謨，夙達先照，惠政茂譽，實留民屬。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, while traveling on tour he passed Jingren's tomb. An edict said, "Minister of Works Duke Wen of Cheng Jingren's virtue and measure were deep and upright, his bearing and insight clear and trustworthy. His fine achievements and loyal counsel were understood early and shone beforehand. His benevolent governance and abundant reputation truly remain with the people.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Shizu, while traveling on tour he passed Yin Jingren's tomb. An edict said, "Minister of Works Duke Wen of Cheng Yin Jingren's virtue and measure were deep and upright, his bearing and insight clear and trustworthy. His fine achievements and loyal counsel were understood early and shone beforehand. His benevolent governance and abundant reputation truly remain with the people.

sentences.zh: 近瞻丘墳，感往興悼，可遣使致祭。」

translations.literal: Gazing recently upon his mound and tomb, I am moved by the past and stirred to mourning. An envoy may be sent to perform sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Gazing recently upon his mound and tomb, I am moved by the past and stirred to mourning. An envoy may be sent to perform sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 子道矜，幼而不慧，官至太中大夫。

translations.literal: His son Daojin was dull from youth and rose to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin Daojin was dull from youth and rose to the post of Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 道矜子恆，太宗世為侍中，度支尚書，屬父疾積久，為有司所奏。

translations.literal: Daojin's son Heng, during Taizong's reign, served as Gentleman Attendant and Director of the Department of Revenue. Because his father's illness had long accumulated, he was impeached by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Daojin's son Yin Heng, during Emperor Taizong's reign, served as Gentleman Attendant and Director of the Department of Revenue. Because his father's illness had long accumulated, he was impeached by the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「道矜生便有病，無更橫疾。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Daojin has been ill from birth and has no further sudden illness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Yin Daojin has been ill from birth and has no further sudden illness.

sentences.zh: 恆因愚習惰，久妨清序，可降為散騎常侍。」

translations.literal: Heng, through foolishness and habitual laziness, has long obstructed proper order. He may be demoted to Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Heng, through foolishness and habitual laziness, has long obstructed proper order. He may be demoted to Regular Attendant of the Dispersed Cavalry."

sentences.zh: 沈演之，字台真，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Yanzhi, courtesy name Taizhen, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanzhi, whose courtesy name was Taizhen, came from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 高祖充，晉車騎將軍，吳國內史。

translations.literal: His ancestor Chong was General of Chariots and Cavalry under Jin and Interior Minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Shen Chong had served as General of Chariots and Cavalry under the Jin dynasty and Interior Minister of Wu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖勁，冠軍陳祐長史，戍金墉城，為鮮卑慕容恪所陷，不屈節，見殺，追贈東陽太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jin was Chief Administrator to Champion Chen You, garrisoning the city of Jinyong. He was captured by the Xianbei Murong Ke, refused to submit, and was killed. Posthumously he was granted Administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shen Jin served as chief administrator to Champion Chen You, garrisoning the city of Jinyong. He was captured by the Xianbei Murong Ke, refused to submit, and was killed. Posthumously he was granted Administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 祖赤黔，廷尉卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chiqian was Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shen Chiqian served as Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 父叔任，少有幹質，初為揚州主簿，高祖太尉參軍，吳、山陰令，治皆有聲。

translations.literal: His father Shuren in youth had capacity and substance. At first he was Chief Clerk of Yangzhou, Adjutant to Gaozu when he was Grand Commandant, and Magistrate of Wu and Shanyin. In each post his governance won renown.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen Shuren in youth showed capacity and substance. He first served as chief clerk of Yangzhou, adjutant to Emperor Gaozu when he held the post of Grand Commandant, and magistrate of Wu and Shanyin. In each post his governance won renown.

sentences.zh: 朱齡石伐蜀，為齡石建威府司馬，加建威將軍。

translations.literal: When Zhu Lingshi campaigned against Shu, Shuren served as Marshal on Lingshi's Establishing Might headquarters and was additionally made General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Lingshi campaigned against Shu, Shen Shuren served as marshal on Lingshi's Establishing Might headquarters and was additionally made General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 平蜀之功，亞于元帥，即本號為西夷校尉、巴西梓潼郡太守，戍涪城。

translations.literal: In the achievement of pacifying Shu his merit was second only to the commander-in-chief. On the basis of his original title he was made Colonel of the Western Yi, Administrator of the commanderies of Baxi and Zitong, and garrisoned Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the achievement of pacifying Shu his merit was second only to the commander-in-chief. On the basis of his original title he was made Colonel of the Western Yi, Administrator of the commanderies of Baxi and Zitong, and garrisoned Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 東軍既反，二郡強宗侯勱、羅奧聚眾作亂，四面雲合，遂至萬餘人，攻城急。

translations.literal: Once the eastern army had rebelled, the powerful clans of the two commanderies, Hou Mo and Luo Ao, gathered followers and raised rebellion. From all four sides they converged like clouds until they reached more than ten thousand men, pressing the siege urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Once the eastern army had rebelled, the powerful clans of the two commanderies, Hou Mo and Luo Ao, gathered followers and raised rebellion. From all four sides they converged like clouds until they reached more than ten thousand men, pressing the siege urgently.

sentences.zh: 叔任東兵不滿五百，推布腹心，眾莫不為用，出擊大破之，逆黨皆平。

translations.literal: Shuren's eastern troops numbered fewer than five hundred. He extended trust with open heart, and none among the men failed to serve him. Going out he attacked and inflicted a great defeat. The rebel faction was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shuren's eastern troops numbered fewer than five hundred. He extended trust with open heart, and none among the men failed to serve him. Going out he attacked and inflicted a great defeat. The rebel faction was entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 高祖討司馬休之，齡石遣叔任率軍來會。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi, Lingshi sent Shuren to lead troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi, Zhu Lingshi sent Shen Shuren to lead troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 時高祖領鎮西將軍，命為司馬。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu held the title General Who Guards the West and appointed Shuren Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Gaozu held the title General Who Guards the West and appointed Shen Shuren marshal.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，以為揚州別駕從事史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Shuren was made Attendant Clerk and Assistant Director of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Shen Shuren was made attendant clerk and assistant director of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以平蜀全涪之功，封寧新縣男，食邑四百四十戶。

translations.literal: For the achievement of pacifying Shu and preserving Fucheng intact, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningxin with a fief of four hundred forty households.
translations.idiomatic: For the achievement of pacifying Shu and preserving Fucheng intact, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Ningxin with a fief of four hundred forty households.

sentences.zh: 出為建威將軍、益州刺史，以疾還都。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yizhou, then returned to the capital because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Yizhou, then returned to the capital because of illness.

sentences.zh: 義熙十四年，卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he died at the age of fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yixi he died at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 長子融之，蚤卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Rongzhi died young.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shen Rongzhi died young.

sentences.zh: 演之年十一，尚書僕射劉柳見而知之，曰：「此童終為令器。

translations.literal: When Yanzhi was eleven, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Liu saw him and recognized his talent, saying, "This boy will in the end become a fine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Yanzhi was eleven, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Liu saw him and recognized his talent, saying, "This boy will in the end become a fine vessel.

sentences.zh: 」家世為將，而演之折節好學，讀《老子》日百遍，以義理業尚知名。

translations.literal: " His family for generations had been generals, but Yanzhi restrained himself and loved learning. He read the Laozi a hundred times each day and became renowned for his pursuit of principle and reason.
translations.idiomatic: " His family for generations had been generals, but Shen Yanzhi restrained himself and loved learning. He read the Laozi a hundred times each day and became renowned for his pursuit of principle and reason.

sentences.zh: 襲父別爵吉陽縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's separate noble rank as Fifth-Rank Marquis of Jiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's separate noble rank as Fifth-Rank Marquis of Jiyang County.

sentences.zh: 郡命主簿，州辟從事史，西曹主簿，舉秀才，嘉興令，有能名。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed him Chief Clerk. The province recruited him as Attendant Clerk, then as Chief Clerk of the Western Section. He was recommended as a Filial and Incorrupt candidate, became Magistrate of Jiaxing, and won a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery appointed him chief clerk. The province recruited him as attendant clerk, then as chief clerk of the western section. He was recommended as a Filial and Incorrupt candidate, became Magistrate of Jiaxing, and won a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 入為司徒祭酒，南譙王義宣左軍主簿，錢唐令，復有政績。

translations.literal: He entered court as Libationer of the Minister of Education, then served as Left Army Chief Clerk to Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan and as Magistrate of Qiantang, again achieving administrative merit.
